The fragmentation of global trade, driven by US-China tensions and the rise of geoeconomic blocs, is likely to continue reshaping supply chains. In this context, emerging markets with strategic locations and trade agreements across multiple blocs, such as India, Saudi Arabia, Mexico, Brazil, the UAE, and Southeast Asia, are expected to thrive. India is likely to strengthen its trade relations across geopolitical divides and drive South-South trade, while Southeast Asia is expected to remain a leading destination for foreign investment among emerging markets. Ongoing advancements in AI and digital technologies are set to revolutionise industries globally, with innovations like DeepSeek's efficient large language model potentially lowering adoption barriers. For India, this emphasises the need for introspection, focusing on affordable, scalable, and collaborative AI development to strengthen local capabilities. While risks posed by potential U.S. trade policies are real and are expected to impact Asia's overall growth outlook, India remains less vulnerable due to its low goods exports as a share of GDP. This reduces its exposure to global trade disruptions. At the same time, India's services exports continue to perform well and are expected to grow further, providing stability amid global uncertainties. Domestically, the translation of order books of private capital goods sector into sustained investment pick-up, improvements in consumer confidence, and corporate wage pick-up will be key to promoting growth. multiple blocs, such as India, Saudi Arabia, Mexico, 
Brazil, the UAE, and Southeast Asia, are expected to 
thrive. India is likely to strengthen its trade relations 
across geopolitical divides and drive South-South trade, 
while Southeast Asia is expected to remain a leading 
destination for foreign investment among emerging 
markets. Ongoing advancements in AI and digital 
technologies are set to revolutionise industries globally, 
with innovations like DeepSeek's efficient large 
language model potentially lowering adoption barriers. 
For India, this emphasises the need for introspection, 
focusing on affordable, scalable, and collaborative AI 
development to strengthen local capabilities.
 
Economic prospects for India in 2025 look balanced and 
most agencies forecast an encouraging picture of 
India's economy in the coming year. While risks posed 
by potential U.S. trade policies are real and are 
expected to impact Asia's overall growth outlook, India 
remains less vulnerable due to its low goods exports as 
a share of GDP. This reduces its exposure to global 
trade disruptions. At the same time, India's services 
exports continue to perform well and are expected to 
grow further, providing stability amid global 
uncertainties. Domestically, the translation of order 
books of private capital goods sector into sustained 
investment pick-up, improvements in consumer 
confidence, and corporate wage pick-up will be key to 
promoting growth. Real GDP growth in FY26 is 
expected to range between 6.3% — 6.8%, factoring in 
both upside and downside risks. Rural demand backed 
by a rebound in agricultural production, an anticipated 
easing of food inflation and a stable macroeconomic 
environment provide an upside to near-term growth. In

2025, with an average of around 3.2% expected over 
the next five years – a pace considered modest by

remains steady, growth paths diverge significantly 
across regions.
For India too, growth momentum encountered 
headwinds in the first quarter of FY25, largely attributed 
to the general election and a dip in capital expenditure. 
Nevertheless, the nation's growth trajectory proved 
resilient, albeit moderating, with provisional MoSPI 
estimates showing FY25 GDP growth at 6.5% – the 
slowest since the pandemic-affected FY21. A strong 
fourth quarter rebound, recording 7.4% GDP growth, 
was crucial in lifting the annual figures, though it 
remained below the 8.4% seen in the same quarter 
of the previous year. Sectoral performance varied: 
agriculture made a robust recovery (5.4% in Q4, 4.6% 
annual), manufacturing moderated to 4.5% annually, 
and construction saw a powerful Q4 resurgence 
(10.8%), contributing to a 9.4% full-year expansion. 
Services sector registered 7.2% growth for the year, 
down from 9% in FY24. Demand-side analysis reveals 
improved private consumption growth at 7.2%, 
reflecting increased household spending, even as 
capital formation growth eased to 7.1%, indicating a 
moderation in investment activity despite a year-end 
boost. Crucially, India's macroeconomic stability 
endured, underpinned by strong fiscal discipline, a 
thriving services trade surplus, and robust remittance 
inflows. The RBI's measured monetary policy has been 
instrumental in inflation management, while widespread 
infrastructure development continues to boost 
connectivity and economic dynamism. The growing 
digital economy further strengthens this foundation, 
fostering innovation and inclusion, thereby enabling 
sustained growth despite external uncertainties.

intensified uncertainties surrounding the economic 
outlook globally, creating new challenges for growth and 
inflation. In response, central banks are proceeding 
cautiously, with policy divergence becoming apparent 
Macro Economic Review and Outlook
Globally, 2024 has been an eventful year. The year 
witnessed significant electoral activity and saw over half 
the world's population participate in major elections, 
triggering significant policy volatility as newly elected 
governments implemented swift domestic and 
international strategy shifts. These elections, coupled 
with heightened geopolitical tensions, reshaped 
international alliances, creating both opportunities and 
challenges for global stability. Notably, the return of the 
Trump administration in the US intensified this volatility, 
instigating a marked shift towards protectionist trade 
policies. The imposition of "reciprocal" tariffs by the US, 
designed to mirror those of other nations, fuelled 
concerns about escalating trade tensions and supply 
chain disruptions. Consequently, market volatility 
increased, and nations were compelled to reassess 
established trade and diplomatic relationships, 
navigating a more fragmented and unpredictable 
global landscape.
Amidst these complexities of geoeconomic 
fragmentation, tariff disputes, and persistent global 
uncertainties, India has demonstrated remarkable 
resilience. Through a combination of inherent 
dynamism, strategic policy interventions, and a well-calibrated foreign affairs approach, India has not 
only navigated the challenging landscape but also 
solidified its position as a pivotal force in the evolving 
global economic order. This adept navigation, built upon 
a foundation of structural reforms and sustainable 
development, has enabled India to forge ahead while 
others have experienced setbacks.
Looking back at 2024, the global economic environment 
was marked by a gradual moderation of inflationary 
pressures, though many advanced economies still 
grappled with elevated price levels. Geopolitical 
tensions persisted, contributing to supply chain 
disruptions and market volatility. Central banks globally 
adopted a cautious monetary policy stance, balancing 
the need to curb inflation with the imperative of 
supporting economic growth. Recent strength in the US 
dollar and rethinking in the Federal Reserve about the 
path of policy rates in America have caused emerging 
market currencies to weaken. Fiscal strains and low real 
rates relative to history have led to rapid erosion of value 
in some currencies compared to others. Borrowing 
costs for sovereigns are also rising as financial markets 
re-evaluate the outlook for inflation, policy rates and 
fiscal prudence. Looking ahead, the International DDiissccuussssiioonn  &&

sector, and regulatory reforms. Overall, India 
will need to improve its global competitiveness through grassroots-level structural reforms and deregulation to reinforce its medium-term growth potential. The expansion of the manufacturing sector, driven by initiatives like "Make in India" and PLI schemes, is expected to gain momentum. The growing middle class and rising disposable incomes will continue to fuel consumption and retail growth. The services sector, particularly in IT, digital services, and tourism, holds immense potential for further expansion. Increased exports, driven by global supply chain diversification, and a surge in private sector investment spurred by government infrastructure spending, will further contribute to economic momentum. 
India's remarkable economic growth over the past 
decade has propelled its GDP to $4.3 trillion, solidifying its position as the world's fastest-growing major economy. Projections indicate it will become the third-largest economy globally by overtaking Germany by mid-2027. However, this progress faces headwinds from geopolitical and trade uncertainties, and potential commodity price shocks, necessitating proactive and agile risk management. Persistent inflation above the RBI's target has led to maintained policy rates despite slower recent growth, with rising core inflation posing a risk to consumer demand. Future growth prospects are intertwined with global trends, particularly geopolitical stability and the pace of recovery in the West, as trade disruptions could impact exports. Despite these challenges, India's economic growth is expected to continue its upward trajectory, increasingly aligning with pre-pandemic growth levels.
India is currently experiencing growth divergence, 
trending upwards even as advanced economies slow down. This positive divergence is attributed to strategic domestic interventions boosting India's growth potential, suggesting that with continued right policies, India has the capacity for even faster growth. While macroeconomic health checklist for India looks good, to realise the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 India will need to achieve a growth rate of around 8%, on average, for about a decade or two. As the country aims to accelerate its economic growth rate in the coming years, it has the tailwind of strong balance sheets in the domestic corporate and financial sectors. But, with globalisation on the retreat, raising the average growth in the next two decades might require reaping the demographic dividend through a deregulation stimulus. 
Industry Structure and Developments 
Alternative Asset Management
The asset management industry in India comprises of 
Alternative Asset Management and Mutual Funds.India has witnessed a shift in investment and savings trends from conventional options like Bank FDs to  Mutual Funds and Alternative Investments. This change is driven by increasing financial literacy, higher income India's remarkable economic growth over the 
past decade has propelled its GDP to $4.3 trillion, 
solidifying its position as the world's fastest-
growing major economy. Projections indicate it 
will become the third-largest economy globally 
by overtaking Germany by mid-2027. 
levels, regulatory support, and the desire for better returns. The growth of digital platforms and easy access to information have also contributed to this shift, enabling investors to explore and invest in diverse asset classes.Alternative Asset Management can be classified as 
Public alternatives (hedge funds, concentrated public equity strategies), Private Alternatives (Real Assets, Private Credit, Private Equity) and Perpetual Strategies (InvITs and REITs). 
The number of High-Net-Worth Individuals (HNIs) and 
Ultra-High-Net-Worth Individuals (UHNIs) is expected to double by 2027 compared to 2022. Additionally, the increasing corpus of pension funds and insurance companies is expected to provide a substantial pool of capital actively seeking alternative investment options. This is expected to translate into significant growth potential for income and yield products like Real Assets and Private Credit in India.
Within India's Private Alternatives investment landscape, 
over the last decade Real Assets and Private Credit have provided investors superior risk-adjusted returns leading to development of this market. India's projected GDP growth towards $6.7 trillion by 2029 presents a massive $247 billion opportunity for Alternative Assets, creating an attractive investment environment. Within this, Real Assets and Private Credit in India are expected to reach ~46% of the Indian Alternatives market by 2029 to $114 billion, leading the industry's growth. (source: IMF and Preqin)
Real Assets funds focus on development and 
monetisation of assets to release productive capital in the country and are a large investment opportunity. This exceptional growth trajectory positions India's Private Alternative investment space as a preeminent destination for investors seeking risk-adjusted, long-term, high-potential returns.
Private Credit funds look to provide flexible financing 
solutions for meeting the growth and refinancing requirements for the corporates India. They are becoming an integral part of the financial ecosystem and are playing an important role in development of debt markets in India. Private Credit delivered through Private Alternative funds with matched asset-liability structures solves a tangible problem for the borrowers. 
Mutual Funds
India's Mutual Fund industry is also making significant strides, characterised by consistent growth and promising indicators. With a strong track record of performance and a diverse range of investment options, it is well-positioned to meet the needs of various investors. In FY25, Mutual Funds Industry AUM grew 23%, reaching `65.74 trillion as of 31 March 2025, 
compared to `53.40 trillion as of 31 March 2024. (Source: AMFI reports). This growth is fuelled by a combination of factors, 
including the rising financial literacy among the populace, favourable performance of the stock market, and the convenience of digital investing. Notably, there is a rising involvement of young Indians in equity investments, driven by the desire to build wealth in a changing economic landscape. Technology has played a pivotal role in democratising access to mutual funds, offering simplified processes and user-friendly platforms that make investing more accessible to a wider audience.
Looking forward, the outlook for India's mutual funds 
industry remains promising. With ample opportunities for expansion and the potential to attract new investors, the industry is poised for further growth. As more participants enter the market and innovative products emerge, we anticipate an exciting journey of wealth creation and financial empowerment. While challenges may arise, the resilience and adaptability of India's

137 138Annual Report 2024-25 Management Discussion & Analysis Edelweiss Financial Services Limited
Asset Reconstruction 
The ARC industry in India is operating within a 
strengthened regulatory framework emphasising transparency and accountability. The RBI's focus on equitable settlement practices, underscored by mandatory reviews for high-value cases and stringent board oversight, aims to enhance trust and efficiency in distressed asset resolution. 
CRISIL, in its report, projects that Asset Reconstruction 
Companies (ARCs) will see the cumulative recovery rate of security receipts (SRs) increase for the second consecutive year, rising by up to 15% points annually to reach 75–80% by the next fiscal year. This improvement is driven by three main factors: strong performance of stressed assets in key infrastructure sectors such as real estate, thermal power, and roads; a higher proportion of retail and low-vintage assets; and slower growth in new acquisitions relative to incremental recoveries.
Additionally, better performance of stressed 
infrastructure assets, coupled with the deterrent impact of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC), is encouraging debt restructuring, which is becoming the preferred resolution method. The growing acquisition of retail loan portfolios is also supporting recovery rates, with cumulative ARC recoveries for these assets expected to reach 60–65% next fiscal (about 8% of total recoveries), up from 55–60% this fiscal. This is attributed to faster churn and shorter redemption periods of 2.5–4 years for retail loans, compared to 5–6 years for corporate assets.
The growth outlook for ARCs in 2025 presents distinct 
nuances between the wholesale and retail segments. While successful resolution of large corporate NPAs can lead to substantial individual recoveries, growth in the retail and SME sectors hinges on efficiently managing a higher volume of smaller accounts, demanding robust technological infrastructure and widespread collection capabilities. ARCs focusing on wholesale assets may experience growth in spurts tied to significant deals, while those prioritising retail and SME portfolios could see more consistent, incremental growth. Ultimately, the ability of ARCs to strategically navigate these diverse market segments, adapt to the evolving regulatory environment, and leverage technological advancements will be crucial determinants of their sustained growth and value creation within the Indian financial ecosystem.
MSME FinanceThe MSME sector has emerged as a highly vibrant and dynamic sector of the Indian economy over the last five decades and is expected to play a significant role in  India's growth story. The MSME sector plays a crucial role and continues to be a cornerstone of India's economic growth, contributing significantly to employment, manufacturing, and exports, accounting for over 30% of India's GDP and is expected to contribute to over 40% of the GDP by FY30. 
The Union Budget 2025-26 introduces a series of 
measures aimed at strengthening the MSME sector by enhancing credit access, supporting first-time entrepreneurs, and promoting labour-intensive industries. Formal credit deployment will play a crucial role in the growth of this sector and NBFCs will be a critical contributor. Between FY19 and FY21, secured MSME disbursements witnessed a decline from `2.01 
trillion to `1.55 trillion, after bouncing back in FY22 and increasing to `3.29 trillion as of FY23 and `4.04 trillion in FY24. Secured MSME portfolio (<`5 million) is expected to grow at 18-20% CAGR from FY24 to FY27. 
Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) have 
emerged as crucial pillars in the Indian financial landscape, offering alternative financing solutions to a wide array of borrowers. Unlike traditional banks, NBFCs possess the agility to address the nuanced financial needs of underserved segments, including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and self-employed individuals. NBFCs have played a significant role in fostering entrepreneurship, enabling business expansion, and ultimately promoting financial inclusion. The deep understanding of regional markets and customer-centric approach have further solidified the position as enablers of inclusive economic growth.
Here are the key updates for the industry:
The Union Budget 2025-26 introduced series of measures aimed at strengthening the MSME sector by enhancing credit access, supporting first-time entrepreneurs, and promoting labour-intensive industries. To help MSMEs scale operations and access better resources, the investment and turnover limits for classification have been increased by 2.5 times and 2 times, respectively. This is expected to improve efficiency, technological adoption, and employment generation.With the RBI reducing the repo rate, banks have started passing on the benefits of lower rates resulting in reduced borrowing costs for NBFCs.
The MSME budget allocation has seen consistent growth, with `23,168 crore allocated in FY26.

by strong domestic demand and accelerated expansion 
in both manufacturing and services sectors. This positive

sectors present compelling investment opportunities,

139 140Annual Report 2024-25 Management Discussion & Analysis Edelweiss Financial Services Limited
The Indian general insurance sector recorded muted 
year-on-year growth of 6.2% in FY25, a significant slowdown from the 13% growth seen in the previous year. This moderation reflects a more cautious market environment, though the industry remained committed to aligning with the IRDAI's vision of a transparent, inclusive, and technology-driven ecosystem. Insurers continued to focus on reducing operational inefficiencies, maintaining cost discipline, and enhancing customer service.
Private general insurers maintained their leadership 
position with a stable market share of around 53%. Standalone Health Insurers (SAHI) expanded their presence, increasing market share to 12.5% from 11.4% last year, driven by rising demand for retail health products. Public sector insurers retained their market share at 31.0%, while specialised PSU insurers experienced a slight decline to 3.6%.Motor insurance grew by 7.9% YoY, supported by volume growth; however, insurers faced margin pressure due to pricing competition and rising repair costs. Health insurance reported robust growth of 11.2%, primarily led by retail demand. At the same time, the push for regulatory standardisation added stress to underwriting margins and loss ratios. The Property Insurance segment saw a 2.4% decline, affected by premium rate softening and increased competitive intensity. Crop insurance, despite a 2.0% contraction, continued to contribute approximately 10% of total industry premiums, remaining a strategically significant line of business due to its rural outreach and EOM (End-Of-Month) benefits.
FY25 witnessed several key regulatory shifts. These 
included liberalisation in product offerings, strengthened policyholder protection norms, and expanded coverage mandates in health insurance. Additionally, the industry began preparations for adopting Ind AS 117, the new insurance accounting standard. Insurers initiated system alignments and operational updates to ensure a smooth transition and regulatory compliance.
The Indian general insurance industry remains 
fundamentally resilient. Regulatory reforms introduced during FY25 are expected to enhance governance structures, improve customer outcomes, and strengthen the sector's long-term sustainability. Continued investment in digital infrastructure, innovation, and customer-centric practices will be critical in navigating future growth opportunities.
year-on-year rise of approximately 6.8% in Q2FY25, 
compared to 4.9% in the same period the previous year, which reflects an ongoing confidence in the housing market from both buyers and lenders. Key drivers include robust economic fundamentals, with GDP growth projected at 6.8–7% in FY25, affordable interest rates, and rapid urbanisation. Post-pandemic shifts toward homeownership continue to propel demand, with public sector banks and HFCs ensuring credit availability. 
The expansion of HFCs into deeper geographies, 
including Tier 2 and 3 cities, and the policy momentum through PMAY 2.0, UIDF, ARHC scheme and land record digitisation, point towards a future where financial access is frictionless. The Housing Finance industry is leveraging technology like never before, enhancing efficiency and customer experience. Innovation in green housing, digital underwriting, and co-lending frameworks is inevitable going forward. With risk management and customer-centric innovation, housing finance will continue to be at the forefront of India's financial deepening story — not just by the square footage built but by lives uplifted and communities empowered.

Life Insurance
The life insurance sector remained on its growth 
trajectory, supported by the vast market opportunity, rising affluence, increased adoption of technology and low penetration levels. The new business premiums collected by the industry closed short of the `4-trillion 
mark, recording 5% YoY growth. Additionally, the 
individual APE jumped 10% YoY. The private sector continued to claim a higher market share, closing the financial year with 71% of the pie, up from 68% in the previous financial year.
The evolving regulatory landscape remained the 
predominant industry driver, with IRDAI announcing significant reforms around surrender values, products, and more for the protection of policyholders' interests. 
  The industry continued its efforts towards improving 
awareness, with focused efforts under the State Insurance Plan, and accessibility through strategic partnerships as well as expansion of advisor base. The industry added more than 1.1 million new individual life insurance agents in FY25, recording a near 8% growth in the cumulative agent count.
The financial year gone by also saw significant M&A 
activity; Aegon Life rebranded as Bandhan Life following exit of Bennett Coleman Group, Max Life rebranded as Axis Max Life Insurance after Axis Bank increased its stake, and Allianz Group announced its exit from both insurance joint ventures with Bajaj Finserv. With low penetration levels, India continues to present vast market opportunity. As per Swiss Re, India is touted to become the fastest-growing among G20 nations over the next five years.

The government's push for financial inclusion, coupled with an increasingly digital-first economy, presents a promising outlook for the industry. Insurers initiated system alignments and operational updates to ensure a smooth transition and regulatory compliance.
The Indian general insurance industry remains 
fundamentally resilient. Regulatory reforms introduced during FY25 are expected to enhance governance structures, improve customer outcomes, and strengthen the sector's long-term sustainability. Continued investment in digital infrastructure, innovation, and customer-centric practices will be critical in navigating future growth opportunities.

Key drivers include robust economic fundamentals, with GDP growth projected at 6.8–7% in FY25, affordable interest rates, and rapid urbanisation. Post-pandemic shifts toward homeownership continue to propel demand, with public sector banks and HFCs ensuring credit availability. 
The expansion of HFCs into deeper geographies,

General Insurance
Life Insurance
The life insurance sector remained on its growth trajectory, supported by the vast market opportunity, rising affluence, increased adoption of technology and low penetration levels. The new business premiums collected by the industry closed short of the `4-trillion 
mark, recording 5% YoY growth. Additionally, the 
individual APE jumped 10% YoY. The private sector continued to claim a higher market share, closing the financial year with 71% of the pie, up from 68% in the previous financial year.
The evolving regulatory landscape remained the 
predominant industry driver, with IRDAI announcing significant reforms around surrender values, products, and more for the protection of policyholders' interests. 
  The industry continued its efforts towards improving 
awareness, with focused efforts under the State Insurance Plan, and accessibility through strategic partnerships as well as expansion of advisor base. The industry added more than 1.1 million new individual life insurance agents in FY25, recording a near 8% growth in the cumulative agent count.
The financial year gone by also saw significant M&A 
activity; Aegon Life rebranded as Bandhan Life following exit of Bennett Coleman Group, Max Life rebranded as Axis Max Life Insurance after Axis Bank increased its stake, and Allianz Group announced its exit from both insurance joint ventures with Bajaj Finserv. With low penetration levels, India continues to present vast market opportunity. As per Swiss Re, India is touted to become the fastest-growing among G20 nations over the next five years.

139 140Annual Report 2024-25 Management Discussion & Analysis Edelweiss Financial Services Limited
The Indian general insurance sector recorded muted 
year-on-year growth of 6.2% in FY25, a significant 
slowdown from the 13% growth seen in the previous 
year. This moderation reflects a more cautious market 
environment, though the industry remained committed 
to aligning with the IRDAI's vision of a transparent, 
inclusive, and technology-driven ecosystem. Insurers 
continued to focus on reducing operational 
inefficiencies, maintaining cost discipline, and 
enhancing customer service.
Private general insurers maintained their leadership 
position with a stable market share of around 53%. 
Standalone Health Insurers (SAHI) expanded their 
presence, increasing market share to 12.5% from 
11.4% last year, driven by rising demand for retail 
health products. Public sector insurers retained their 
market share at 31.0%, while specialised PSU 
insurers experienced a slight decline to 3.6%.Motor insurance grew by 7.9% YoY, supported by 
volume growth; however, insurers faced margin 
pressure due to pricing competition and rising repair 
costs. Health insurance reported robust growth of 
11.2%, primarily led by retail demand. At the same time, 
the push for regulatory standardisation added stress to 
underwriting margins and loss ratios. The Property 
Insurance segment saw a 2.4% decline, affected by 
premium rate softening and increased competitive 
intensity. Crop insurance, despite a 2.0% contraction, 
continued to contribute approximately 10% of total 
industry premiums, remaining a strategically significant 
line of business due to its rural outreach and EOM (End-
Of-Month) benefits.
FY25 witnessed several key regulatory shifts. These 
included liberalisation in product offerings, strengthened 
policyholder protection norms, and expanded coverage 
mandates in health insurance. Additionally, the industry 
began preparations for adopting Ind AS 117, the new 
insurance accounting standard. Insurers initiated system 
alignments and operational updates to ensure a smooth 
transition and regulatory compliance.

fundamentally resilient. Regulatory reforms introduced 
during FY25 are expected to enhance governance 
structures, improve customer outcomes, and strengthen 
the sector's long-term sustainability. Continued

customer-centric practices will be critical in navigating

141 142The Way Forward
FY25 was a pivotal year for the Group, marked by 
strategic milestones, strong operating performance across businesses, and disciplined financial management. The year was marked by consistent performance and growth across our core businesses, particularly in Alternative Asset Management, Mutual Fund, and Asset Reconstruction. Notably, our insurance segment gained strong momentum, placing them firmly on the path towards break-even. Over the past three years, we've reduced consolidated net debt by ~40% and have brought down our legacy wholesale book in ECL Finance by ~`8,000 crore. Our robust, well-
capitalised balance sheet continues to support 
our efforts to systematically reduce corporate net debt.
Looking ahead to FY26, our strategic focus is on 
enhancing profitability in our high-growth Alternative Asset Management and Mutual Fund businesses, while strategically expanding our retail credit footprint through an asset-light Co-Lending Model. We are equally committed to ensuring the long-term sustainability and profitability of our insurance businesses, targeting break-even in both of our Insurance businesses by FY27. Our ongoing initiatives aimed at net debt reduction will persist, ensuring continued financial flexibility and stability as we progress.
In response to the evolving market dynamics, our 
strategic approach remains adaptable. With a clearly defined set of priorities for the upcoming year, we are well-positioned to navigate market shifts, generate value for our stakeholders, and reinforce our leadership within the financial sector.Opportunities 
The financial services sector is poised for robust growth, 
driven by rapid technological innovation, evolving regulatory frameworks, and shifting consumer profiles. These interwoven trends are not merely reshaping the industry; they are forging pathways to remarkable growth and success. capture new opportunities that will contribute to the growth of India's financial ecosystem. 
In the coming year, our strategic focus will continue to 
remain on enhancing value in our underlying businesses, optimising capital structures, and harnessing emerging technologies to innovate and navigate market fluctuations. By leveraging our expertise and forward-looking approach, we are prepared to capitalise on emerging trends. Our steadfast dedication to identifying and fostering growth opportunities reinforces our commitment to unlocking substantial value for our stakeholders.
A wave of transformative technologies is redefining how financial products are developed, delivered, and experienced. Artificial Intelligence (AI), blockchain, and cloud computing are no longer futuristic concepts —they are the core drivers of innovation today. AI enables hyper-personalised financial solutions, intelligent automation, and predictive risk management. Blockchain is streamlining transactions and increasing transparency, while cloud platforms are improving scalability and operational agility. Together, these technologies are not just optimising existing systems — they're opening entirely new frontiers for value creation.Tech Revolution: AI, Blockchain, and Cloud Forge New Frontiers.
Expanding mobile penetration and proactive government initiatives are helping integrate previously underserved populations into the formal financial ecosystem. This is unlocking new growth opportunities across credit, insurance, and digital payment solutions, especially in rural and semi-urban areas.Financial Inclusion: Expanding Access, Unlocking Growth
Demographic Dividend: A Young, Affluent, and Digital-First Population
India's demographic shift is transforming the financial 
landscape. A growing middle class and a young, tech-savvy population are driving demand for smarter, more accessible, and mobile-first financial solutions. Seamless digital experiences, transparency, and personalisation are no longer added features, they are essential expectations. Financial services must evolve rapidly to keep pace with this new wave of digital-native consumers.
Sustainable Prosperity: ESG Moves to the Mainstream 
Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) considerations are increasingly influencing investment decisions. There is rising demand for green finance, ethical investing, and socially responsible lending. Institutions are aligning their products and policies with broader climate and social goals — recognising that sustainability is not only a moral imperative but also a driver of long-term business success.Threats
While the financial services sector is ripe with opportunity, it also faces a complex landscape of risks that require 
continuous monitoring and adaptability.
Cybersecurity and 
Technological Risks
The increasing reliance on digital 
infrastructure and advanced technologies exposes institutions to evolving cyber threats — ranging from data breaches and AI-powered attacks to vulnerabilities in third-party platforms. Strengthening cybersecurity measures, investing in threat intelligence, and ensuring regulatory compliance are critical to maintaining trust and resilience.Regulatory Uncertainty
As financial innovation outpaces 
traditional regulation, institutions face ongoing uncertainty around evolving frameworks — particularly in areas such as data privacy, digital lending, and ESG reporting. Adapting swiftly to new regulations while maintaining agility in product development will be essential.Macroeconomic and 
Geopolitical Volatility
Fluctuations in interest rates, 
persistent inflation, and global geopolitical tensions continue to impact capital flows, credit quality, and investor sentiment. These uncertainties demand robust stress testing, agile risk management, and diversified portfolio strategies to mitigate potential disruptions.Key challenges include:

they're opening entirely new frontiers for value creation.Tech Revolution: AI, Blockchain, and Cloud Forge New Frontiers.
Expanding mobile penetration and proactive 
government initiatives are helping integrate previously 
underserved populations into the formal financial ecosystem. This is unlocking new growth opportunities 
across credit, insurance, and digital payment solutions, 
especially in rural and semi-urban areas.Financial Inclusion: Expanding Access, Unlocking Growth
Demographic Dividend: A Young, Affluent, and Digital-First Population
India's demographic shift is transforming the financial 
landscape. A growing middle class and a young, 
tech-savvy population are driving demand for smarter, 
more accessible, and mobile-first financial solutions. 
Seamless digital experiences, transparency, and personalisation are no longer added features, they 
are essential expectations. Financial services must 
evolve rapidly to keep pace with this new wave of 
digital-native consumers.
Sustainable Prosperity: ESG Moves to the Mainstream 
Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) 
considerations are increasingly influencing investment 
decisions. There is rising demand for green finance, 
ethical investing, and socially responsible lending. Institutions are aligning their products and policies with 
broader climate and social goals — recognising that 
sustainability is not only a moral imperative but also a 
driver of long-term business success.Threats
While the financial services sector is ripe with opportunity, it also faces a complex landscape of risks that require 
continuous monitoring and adaptability.
Cybersecurity and 
Technological Risks
The increasing reliance on digital 
infrastructure and advanced 
technologies exposes institutions to 
evolving cyber threats — ranging 
from data breaches and AI-powered 
attacks to vulnerabilities in third-
party platforms. Strengthening 
cybersecurity measures, investing in 
threat intelligence, and ensuring 
regulatory compliance are critical to 
maintaining trust and resilience.Regulatory Uncertainty
As financial innovation outpaces 
traditional regulation, institutions 
face ongoing uncertainty around 
evolving frameworks — particularly 
in areas such as data privacy, digital 
lending, and ESG reporting. 
Adapting swiftly to new regulations 
while maintaining agility in product 
development will be essential.Macroeconomic and 
Geopolitical Volatility
Fluctuations in interest rates, 
persistent inflation, and global 
geopolitical tensions continue to 
impact capital flows, credit quality, 
and investor sentiment. These 
uncertainties demand robust stress 
testing, agile risk management, and 
diversified portfolio strategies to 
mitigate potential disruptions.Key challenges include:Annual Report 2024-25 Management Discussion & Analysis Edelweiss Financial Services Limited

interest for FY25 stood at `536 crore. PAT from non-

levels ( `9,602 crore). Interest income declined by 5% 
YoY ( `2,690 crore in FY25 vs `2,832 crore in FY24), 
reflecting our strategic shift toward asset-light models in retail credit and the continued wind-down of the wholesale book. Meanwhile, our insurance businesses continued their growth trajectory, achieving a net premium of `2,620 crore in FY25, up from  `2,278 crore

crore from `9,164 crore in FY24. This reduction was Performance Highlights
Edelweiss is actively evolving — focusing on building 
and scaling multiple independent, high-growth businesses across the financial services landscape. In line with our strategy of creating and unlocking value at the right moment, we successfully completed the sale of our investments in Nuvama during the year. These transactions enhanced consolidated liquidity by ~ `3,250 crore, providing us with surplus liquidity that 
supported further debt reduction and strengthened our 
balance sheet. 
EAAA India Alternatives (EAAA) filed its initial DRHP 
with SEBI on 5 December 2024, for an Offer for Sale of up to `1,500 crore. Following SEBI's observations, a 
revised DRHP will be submitted, with eventual listing 
based on regulatory approvals and market conditions.
Our core businesses delivered strong operating results, 
building on the momentum established in the previous year. The Alternative Asset Management business recorded a robust performance, with AUM increasing by 9% YoY to `59,630 crore. Within this, ARR AUM 
grew by 6% YoY to `45,000 crore, contributing to a 31% YoY increase in profitability. The Mutual Fund 
business also delivered sustained growth, with total AUM rising by 12% YoY to `1,41,800 crore. Equity AUM 
grew by 43%, while profitability increased by 40% to 
`53 crore in FY25. The Insurance segment continued to 
scale effectively, with overall profitability increasing by 
37% YoY. The General Insurance business witnessed a 61% decline in losses YoY whereas Life Insurance business witnessed a ~20% decline in losses. The General Insurance business achieved an exceptional 19% growth in Gross Written Premium (GWP), one of the fastest-growing in the industry, while the Life Insurance business reported a solid 8% growth in Gross Premium to `2,086 crore. 
In the retail credit segment, growth was led by the 
Co-Lending Model. Housing finance disbursements grew by 29% YoY, though profitability remained muted. As disbursement volumes continue to rise and operational capabilities are enhanced, we expect a positive impact on profitability in the coming quarters.During the year, the Reserve Bank of India lifted restrictions on two of our lending entities: Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company (EARC) and ECL Finance Limited. While EARC's profitability was moderately impacted during the restriction period due to limitation on new acquisitions, the impact was offset by strong recoveries. ECL Finance's wholesale lending business remained unaffected, having already been discontinued; however, MSME lending was slightly constrained by lower disbursements. 
primarily driven by a 9% decrease in finance costs, which stood at `2,537 crore compared to `2,786 crore 
in the previous year. Other operating expenses remained flat, indicating improved cost efficiency and scalability. Impairments (including changes in valuation of credit impaired loans) reduced to `507 crore, down 
from `748 crore in FY24. Consolidated debt also saw a 
meaningful reduction — from `18,102 crore in FY24 to 
`15,426 crore in FY25. Throughout the year, we 
maintained adequate liquidity, with available resources averaging approximately 28% of total borrowings. Going forward, our focus remains on further reducing corporate net debt.
The diluted Earnings Per Share (EPS) for FY25 stood at 
`5.81, compared to `4.68 in FY24. Book value per share 
was `47 at the end of FY25. The Board of Directors 
have recommended a final dividend of `1.50 per equity 
share. Total dividend for the year stands at `1.50 per 
equity share.
With surplus capital available in ECL Finance, we undertook a one-time strategic markdown on the SR (Security Receipts) book to accelerate our transition toward SME lending. This decision was made in consultation with the RBI and led to a reduction in the SR book in ECL Finance from `3,400 crore as of 
December 2024 to `2,260 crore in March 2025. Importantly, the markdown does not reflect any 
deterioration in underlying cash flows, and we expect the markdown provision to be recouped and accretive to equity over the next 3–4 years.
Our customer reach expanded further on the back of 
retail scale-up, increasing 36% YoY to 103 lakh customers. This also contributed to a growth in The General Insurance business achieved an 
exceptional 19% growth in Gross Written Premium 
(GWP), one of the fastest-growing in the industry, 
while the Life Insurance business reported an 8% 
growth in Gross Premium to `2,086 Cr.
Liquidity and ALM Proﬁle 
We ensure that an adequate liquidity cushion is maintained to take care of all maturing liabilities with a focus on optimum revenue generation from liquid assets. 
At the end of FY25, we maintained available liquidity 
of `4,255 crore. This included overnight liquid assets 
of `3,425 crore, high-quality liquid assets of over `765 crore which can be liquidated within a short span (if the need arises), and undrawn committed bank credit 
lines of `65 crore.
Over the years, we have demonstrated a strong track 
record of fundraising from both retail and institutional lenders. With the help of public issues and our retail borrowing programmes, we have increased the proportion of funding through retail sources from 45% to 52% in the past one year. 
On the asset side, we continue to focus on and reorient 
our balance sheet towards retail growth. As wholesale recoveries remain slightly slower than anticipated, we have optimised the tenure and focused on medium to long-term borrowings. Long-term borrowings now stand at 74% of the total debt. 
All these steps have ensured that we maintain a positive 
ALM gap across all time buckets.Customer reach expanded further on the back of retail

Analysis of Signiﬁcant Changes in Financial Ratios 
As per the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 below is the additional 
information in respect of the financial parameters that are applicable to our company.
Debt Equity Ratio
The Debt Equity Ratio as on March 31, 2025 
stood at 3.02 times compared to 3.35 times as on 31 March 2024. Including the amount of equity convertible instruments (CCDs) in our networth and excluding the liquid treasury assets that we hold for liquidity management; the Net Gearing Ratio is 1.9 times as on March 2025 compared to 2.5 times as on March 2024.
Details of any changes in Return on Net Worth as compared to the previous financial year:
Return on Net Worth, i.e. Return on Equity (RoE), Post-MI on consolidated basis for FY25 stood at 8.2% compared to 9.2% for FY24.Details of significant changes in key financial ratios: 
Net Profit Margin (%) 
The Profit After Tax Margin for FY25 stood at 5.6% 
compared to 5.5% for FY24.
Profit Before Tax Margin (%) 
The Profit Before Tax Margin for FY25 was 8.4% 
compared to 4.6% in FY24.

Alternative Asset Management
EAAA India Alternatives Limited (EAAA), is one of the 
leading alternatives platforms in India, managing an Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) AUM of `45,000 crore 
as of March 31, 2025. With over 15 years of experience, 
EAAA operates a diversified, multi-strategy platform focusing on Real Assets and Private Credit. We cater to a diverse client base of global and domestic institutional clients, UHNIs, HNIs, and family offices. Even, geographically, our client base is diversified with ~50% of fund commitments coming from India, and rest 50% from offshore investors.Our ARR AUM of the alternative business has grown at a CAGR of 19% over last 3 years. During the year, we have raised `6,615 crore, on the back of growing 
demand for Private alternatives in India. This strong 
business performance helped in the rise of ARR Revenue which rose 18% YoY to `472 crore in FY25 
and a Profit After Tax of `230 crore. With strong governance and focus on robust risk management, the 
total deployment was `9,305 crore, and realisation was 
`8,798 crore across strategies in FY25.Other parameters, namely Debtors Turnover, Inventory Turnover, Interest Coverage Ratio, and Current Ratio, 
are not applicable to our Company.

147 148Annual Report 2024-25 Management Discussion & Analysis Edelweiss Financial Services Limited
Real Assets
EAAA's Real Assets strategy invests in infrastructure 
and commercial real estate assets with low counterparty risk and long residual tenures. The sub-strategies include Infrastructure Yield, Commercial Real Estate Yield, Perpetual Capital (InvIT), and Energy Transition. The maiden Commercial Real Estate Yield fund (RYP) successfully raised `3,820 crore till March 2025, 
marking the largest domestic fundraising for a first-
generation fund. In FY25, we have also launched Energy Transition Fund. Energy Transition Fund offers investors a long-term investment vehicle and opportunity to participate in India's sustainable energy transition. 
Private Credit
EAAA's Private Credit strategy offers tailored credit 
solutions to corporates, projects, or sponsors underserved by traditional credit providers. The sub-strategies include Performing Credit, Special Situations, Real Estate Credit, and Core Credit. In FY25, we launched Special Situation India Fund (SSIF). SSIF seeks to invest in a wide range of investments across Special Situations or stressed/distressed and other allied opportunities including “Special Opportunities” in India as per the fund documents.
EAAA is a scaled and experienced player in the large 
and expanding Indian Real Assets and Private Credit market. We have a diversified, multi-strategy platform offering a wide range of alternative investment products, accompanied by a consistent track record. We serve a diverse and longstanding client base with significant potential to scale their commitments. Our technology-enabled institutional platform, dedicated portfolio operating and management platform, and comprehensive risk management systems further solidify their position. Additionally, EAAA is led by a seasoned management team with extensive industry experience, which contributes to our continued success.
We remain well-positioned for sustained growth in FY26. 
Our strategy encompasses expanding and deepening our client base across geographies by leveraging our in-house coverage team and global distribution platform. We aim to further develop our product offerings, particularly those related to income and yield strategies, and continue to leverage technology to improve our operational efficiency, client experience, and strengthen our competitive position. Additionally, we focus on active asset management by building on our operational capabilities and utilising technology, delivering sustained investment performance, and portfolio differentiation. Furthermore, we aim to strengthen our employee value proposition to attract and retain talent.
Industry Accolades
We have received multiple industry accolades, including 
the "Prestigious Brands of Asia Award" (BARC), Asian Investor Asset Management Awards (India Category, 2024 & 2025), and IVCA Best Overall Performance – Private Credit Fund (2024 & 2025). We ranked among the top Private Debt Fund Raisers (PDI, 2021–2024) and were named a Top 2 India Infrastructure Investor (Infrastructure Investor, 2024). Our innovation was recognised with the GenAI: Initiative of the Year Award (GenAI Conclave 2024), while ETNOW named us Best BFSI Brand (2024), and Equalifi presented us the Operational Thought Leadership Award (2024). We also earned the Asset Management Company of the Year – India (Global Private Banking Innovations Awards 2025) and two Gold Awards from LACP for our annual and global communications reports.
Mutual Fund
At Edelweiss Mutual Fund, our values are centered around creating simple yet innovative solutions that genuinely address the needs of our investors. Our core product philosophy embodies simplicity, boldness, pioneering innovation, and a customer-first approach. We prioritise making complex financial concepts accessible, empowering investors to make confident, informed decisions. Our diverse product portfolio, including equity, debt, balanced, and liquid funds, caters to various financial goals and risk appetites. Committed to innovation, we strive to set industry benchmarks with our inventive solutions, consistently enhancing our offerings to deliver superior value. Our experienced team ensures consistent performance, maintaining our reputation as a top-tier asset management company.
Our growth journey is anchored by a solid foundation 
and driven by three distinct investment capabilities that define our excellence. Our fundamental investing strategies, guided by the FAIR framework, delve deeply into market fundamentals to unearth high-potential opportunities. Our factor-based quantitative investing strategies that leverage comprehensive data analysis to pinpoint lucrative investment opportunities. Lastly our fixed-income strategies, use the CLEAR framework and target high-quality assets that provide sustainable and resilient returns. We have a robust risk management framework serving as a strong foundation in which these aspects are firmly grounded. 
Our exceptional investment team, with over 230 years 
of collective experience, equips us to navigate market complexities and seize opportunities with confidence. Our focus has always been on strengthening our internal investment processes and how they are communicated to customers and distribution partners. This commitment is reflected in our performance, with consistent (Q1/Q2) fund performance for our Long-Only & Hybrid Funds in the 3/5-year horizon.
This dual focus on process excellence and stakeholder 
trust builds strong relationships and amplifies our impact in the investment community and form the bedrock of our sustained growth and success. As a result of these factors, we have established ourselves

149 150Annual Report 2024-25 Management Discussion & Analysis Edelweiss Financial Services Limited
as a trusted and reputable asset management company. 
thWe are the 13  largest AMC in the country and continue 
to be one of the fastest growing among the top 15 
mutual fund houses in the industry. Profitability of this business grew by 40% YoY to `53 crore in FY25.
We manage an AUM of `1.42 lakh crore as on March 2025, a growth of 12% over the AUM of `1.27 lakh crore a year ago. Our AUM ex Bharat Bond reached `83,500 crore as on March 2025, a growth of 27%. Our Equity & Hybrid AUM grew by 43% in FY25 to `62,500 crore in assets, from `43,700 crore as on March 2024. We had the best year ever in equity flows with Gross Equity 
flows of ~`20,000 crore and Net Equity flows of 
~`13,000 crore. This was supported by a strong growth in our SIP book with 69% YoY to `395 crore. We catered to 25.5 lakh active folios in FY25, compared to 
15.5 lakh at the end of FY24, an increase of 64% YoY vs industry growth at 32%.
Edelweiss ARC plays a significant role in managing 
stressed assets in India, with Assets Under Management 
(AUM) currently standing at ~ `14,700 crore. We prioritise 
sound governance, compliance, and risk oversight to 
uphold transparency and build trust — essential in 
navigating the challenges of stressed assets.
EARC uses a multi-pronged approach to resolve 
stressed assets, primarily aiming to 'Revive' or 
'Reconstruct' viable businesses that need additional 
funding. Depending on the specifics of each asset, we 
also consider settlement, enf orcement of security 
interests, and resolution through IBC to achieve the best 
outcomes for stakeholders. We continue to seek out 
potential turnaround situations based on borrowers with 
sound profiles and adequate cash flow and collateral 
backing. Our medium-term strategy involves making 
acquisitions at a steady pace while also exploring 
partnerships with investors, where our initial investment 
can be as low as 2.5% on certain deals, allowing us to 
focus on fee-based income. Our experienced and skilled 
team is a key factor in our strong market position and 
consistent performance over time.
Our acquisitions continue to focus on operating assets 
that have the potential for revival. Acquisition in FY25 
remained subdued due to two key factors. Firstly, the 
RBI directive issued on May 2024 temporarily limited 
new acquisitions until it was lifted in December 2024. 
Secondly, prevailing market conditions presented 
challenges, with a relatively limited pipeline of 
wholesale-distressed assets available for acquisition. 
During the financial year 2024-25, the Company's 
performance relating to the r ecovery was impressive and reflects our conviction and commitment to resolve, 
reconstruct and revive. The Company recovered `5
,730 
crore (including ` 60.52 crore from lending to the 
borrowers of the distressed assets) during the financial 
year. Of the recovery of ` 5,730 crore, ~14% was from 
retail portfolio.
 The Board reviewed and approved the write-down of 
AUM undertaken in line with the policy approved during 
the year, resulting in a net write-down of ` 13,032 crore. 
Of this, ` 8,723 crore pertained to 5:95 trusts, with the 
balance relating to 15:85 trusts, all of which have 
completed 8 years and have been reviewed by the 
Board. This write-down reflected a disciplined approach 
to portfolio management. These adjustments are aligned 
with current recovery projections and the trusts' waterfall 
mechanism. Importantly, this write-down had no adverse 
impact on the Company's profitability, as adequate 
provisions were prudently made earlier through fair 
valuation. This approach reinforces the Company's 
strong financial discipline and ensures that the reported 
results accurately reflect th e underlying asset quality 
without any further impact on earnings.
We have consistently performed well in our retail 
portfolio for the past five years and will continue to
focus on this segment to make our portfolio more 
diverse geographically and in terms of the types of 
assets, enhance the stability of our cash flow, and 
improve our overall valuation. With 100% of Q4FY25 
asset acquisitions coming from retail, the portfolio's 
momentum is clear. Retail assets accounted for 18% 
of the total outstanding capital employed as of 
31 March 2025.

151 152Annual Report 2024-25 Management Discussion & Analysis Edelweiss Financial Services Limited
NBFC
Since inception, our NBFC business has remained 
committed to responsible financial intermediation, contributing to the country's credit ecosystem with a focus on secured and unsecured lending solutions across multiple customer segments. Our product suite is thoughtfully designed with a strong emphasis on addressing customer needs, ensuring relevance and value across every offering. We aim to bridge the credit gap faced by MSMEs by leveraging technology to offer customised and flexible financial solutions to MSMEs. 
In the MSME segment, total disbursements for FY25 
stood at `342 crore, while total AUM of MSME segment 
was `899 crore as of 31 March 2025 and continued to maintain strong asset quality. As a proactive measure 
to accelerate the pivot to SME lending, ECL Finance undertook a one-time markdown on its Security Receipts book, reducing it to `2,260 crore as on 
31 March 2025. This markdown is temporary in nature 
as it does not reflect any deterioration in underlying cash flows, and the provision is expected to be recouped to equity over 3-4 years. Even after this markdown, the company is adequately capitalised with comfortable liquidity cushion. Looking ahead, we anticipate accelerated momentum in disbursement growth and portfolio optimisation-driven by technology, strong partnerships, and rigorous risk management-positioning us as a leading player in MSME lending. We also look forward to expanding our Co-Lending Model (CLM) partnerships to achieve the envisioned disbursement growth through collaboration with various nationalised and private banks, as well as NBFCs. 
With approximately 60 million MSMEs in India 
(registered under Udyam), the sector's total funding requirement is expected to reach `25–30 trillion. We 
aim to expand our market presence in the MSME 
Priority Sector Lending (PSL) segment, capitalising on significant growth prospects and emerging opportunities. Our vision for the MSME sector is to become the most trusted financial partner in the growth journeys of India's micro and small enterprises. To achieve this, we will broaden our range of financial offerings through innovative products and focus on improving operational efficiency. Embracing digital transformation will further enable us to deliver exceptional outcomes. 
Our strategic focus continues to center on MSME 
lending where we are strongly positioned to leverage the opportunities arising from India's dynamic economic growth and the rising demand for credit across both consumer and MSME segments. Regarding our discontinued wholesale lending business, we will continue to scale down the portfolio. Throughout the current fiscal year, we have generated net liquidity through recoveries.
Housing Finance
Nido Home Finance has carved a distinctive position in the Indian housing finance landscape. We work at the intersection of aspiration and access, delivering credit to segments that have traditionally been underserved-salaried individuals without formal income proof, self-employed micro-entrepreneurs, first-time homebuyers in Tier 2 and 3 cities. With simple documentation, doorstep service, and underwriting powered by analytics, we bring formal credit to people who have never dealt with a bank before.
A significant portion of our retail customer base falls 
within the Affordable segment with an average ticket size of `1.6 to `1.7 million in FY25. The affordable 
segment contributes over `1,400 crore to our loan book. We have a presence across 67 branches strategically 
positioned in markets using a hub and spoke model to reach out of larger geographies in and around our branches. We are proud to serve around 21,000 customers. What makes Nido special is that we understand our customer. We don't see them through a traditional risk lens. We go deeper — we look at cash flows, intent, and community reputation. We combine technology with human insight, using both to design credit that's not just accessible but sustainable.
On the lending side, we have chosen to partner smart, 
grow lean and remain agile. We successfully established an asset-light business model. We use co-lending, direct assignment and securitisation as strategic levers to build scale without stretching our balance sheet. In fact, around 60% of our total AUMs are channelled through asset-light instruments, optimising the loan book and balance sheet. This lets us retain customer relationships and origination edge while leveraging the bank's capital and reducing our risk. In FY25, we were able to securitise a pool size of `396 crore via multiple 
transactions with NBFCs and insurance companies. 
On the back of disbursals of `1,703 crore, we ended 
FY25 with an AUM of `4,235 crore, and a loan book of `3,209 crore. As on 31 March 2025, the Net Worth stood at `828 crore and the CRAR at 33.60%. For FY25, gross NPAs and net NPAs stood at 2.17% and 
1.76% respectively. 
The transition from Edelweiss Housing to Nido was a 
deliberate, strategic shift aligned with the structural opportunity we see in India's housing finance space over the next decade. That transition is now behind us. At Nido, we've built an affordable housing business with a robust, capital-efficient model — where origination and distribution are our core engines, and capital is allocated where it generates the most value. It's deeply risk-calibrated and built to scale. With this foundation in place, we are now focused on accelerating growth with discipline and conviction.

grow lean and remain agile. We successfully established an asset-light business model. We use co-lending, direct assignment and securitisation as strategic levers to build scale without stretching our balance sheet. In fact, around 60% of our total AUMs are channelled through asset-light instruments, optimising the loan book and balance sheet. This lets us retain customer relationships and origination edge while leveraging the bank's capital and reducing our risk. In FY25, we were able to securitise a pool size of `396 crore via multiple 
transactions with NBFCs and insurance companies. 
On the back of disbursals of `1,703 crore, we ended 
FY25 with an AUM of `4,235 crore, and a loan book of `3,209 crore. As on 31 March 2025, the Net Worth stood at `828 crore and the CRAR at 33.60%. For FY25, gross NPAs and net NPAs stood at 2.17% and 
1.76% respectively. 
The transition from Edelweiss Housing to Nido was a 
deliberate, strategic shift aligned with the structural opportunity we see in India's housing finance space over the next decade. That transition is now behind us. At Nido, we've built an affordable housing business with a robust, capital-efficient model — where origination and distribution are our core engines, and capital is allocated where it generates the most value. It's deeply risk-calibrated and built to scale. With this foundation in place, we are now focused on accelerating growth with discipline and conviction.

NBFC
Since inception, our NBFC business has remained 
committed to responsible financial intermediation, 
contributing to the country's credit ecosystem with a 
focus on secured and unsecured lending solutions 
across multiple customer segments. Our product suite 
is thoughtfully designed with a strong emphasis on 
addressing customer needs, ensuring relevance and 
value across every offering. We aim to bridge the credit 
gap faced by MSMEs by leveraging technology to offer 
customised and flexible financial solutions to MSMEs. 
In the MSME segment, total disbursements for FY25 
stood at `342 crore, while total AUM of MSME segment 
was `899 crore as of 31 March 2025 and continued to 
maintain strong asset quality. As a proactive measure 
to accelerate the pivot to SME lending, ECL Finance 
undertook a one-time markdown on its Security 
Receipts book, reducing it to `2,260 crore as on 
31 March 2025. This markdown is temporary in nature 
as it does not reflect any deterioration in underlying 
cash flows, and the provision is expected to be 
recouped to equity over 3-4 years. Even after this 
markdown, the company is adequately capitalised 
with comfortable liquidity cushion. Looking ahead, we 
anticipate accelerated momentum in disbursement 
growth and portfolio optimisation-driven by technology, 
strong partnerships, and rigorous risk management-
positioning us as a leading player in MSME lending. 
We also look forward to expanding our Co-Lending Model (CLM) partnerships to achieve the envisioned 
disbursement growth through collaboration with various 
nationalised and private banks, as well as NBFCs. 
With approximately 60 million MSMEs in India 
(registered under Udyam), the sector's total funding 
requirement is expected to reach `25–30 trillion. We 
aim to expand our market presence in the MSME 
Priority Sector Lending (PSL) segment, capitalising 
on significant growth prospects and emerging 
opportunities. Our vision for the MSME sector is to 
become the most trusted financial partner in the 
growth journeys of India's micro and small enterprises. 
To achieve this, we will broaden our range of financial 
offerings through innovative products and focus on 
improving operational efficiency. Embracing digital 
transformation will further enable us to deliver 
exceptional outcomes. 
Our strategic focus continues to center on MSME 
lending where we are strongly positioned to leverage 
the opportunities arising from India's dynamic economic 
growth and the rising demand for credit across both 
consumer and MSME segments. Regarding our 
discontinued wholesale lending business, we will 
continue to scale down the portfolio. Throughout the 
current fiscal year, we have generated net liquidity 
through recoveries.Housing Finance
Nido Home Finance has carved a distinctive position in 
the Indian housing finance landscape. We work at the 
intersection of aspiration and access, delivering credit 
to segments that have traditionally been underserved-
salaried individuals without formal income proof, self-
employed micro-entrepreneurs, first-time homebuyers 
in Tier 2 and 3 cities. With simple documentation, 
doorstep service, and underwriting powered by 
analytics, we bring formal credit to people who have 
never dealt with a bank before.
A significant portion of our retail customer base falls 
within the Affordable segment with an average ticket 
size of `1.6 to `1.7 million  in FY25. The affordable 
segment contributes over `1,400 crore to our loan book. 
We have a presence across 67 branches strategically 
positioned in markets using a hub and spoke model to 
reach out of larger geographies in and around our 
branches. We are proud to serve around 21,000 
customers. What makes Nido special is that we 
understand our customer. We don't see them through 
a traditional risk lens. We go deeper — we look at cash 
flows, intent, and community reputation. We combine 
technology with human insight, using both to design 
credit that's not just accessible but sustainable.
On the lending side, we have chosen to partner smart, 
grow lean and remain agile. We successfully established 
an asset-light business model. We use co-lending, direct assignment and securitisation as strategic levers 
to build scale without stretching our balance sheet. In 
fact, around 60% of our total AUMs are channelled 
through asset-light instruments, optimising the loan 
book and balance sheet. This lets us retain customer 
relationships and origination edge while leveraging the 
bank's capital and reducing our risk. In FY25, we were 
able to securitise a pool size of `396 crore via multiple 
transactions with NBFCs and insurance companies. 
On the back of disbursals of `1,703 crore, we ended 
FY25 with an AUM of `4,235 crore, and a loan book of 
`3,209 crore. As on 31 March 2025, the Net Worth 
stood at `828 crore and the CRAR at 33.60%. For FY25, 
gross NPAs and net NPAs stood at 2.17% and 
1.76% respectively. 
The transition from Edelweiss Housing to Nido was a 
deliberate, strategic shift aligned with the structural 
opportunity we see in India's housing finance space 
over the next decade. That transition is now behind us. 
At Nido, we've built an affordable housing business with

allocated where it generates the most value. It's deeply

153 154Annual Report 2024-25 Management Discussion & Analysis Edelweiss Financial Services Limited
Life Insurance
Against the backdrop of a dynamic macroeconomic 
landscape, and continued regulatory momentum inthe insurance sector, our financial year was one of reaffirmation — of our purpose, our intent, and the values that have always anchored us. 
Guided by a growth mindset and our purpose of 
protecting people's dreams and aspirations, we continued to focus on strengthening distribution, personalisation & enhancing customer experience. We reported a 12% jump in Individual APE at `575 crore at 
the end of FY25, outpacing the industry growth of 10%. 
Since inception, our Individual APE has grown at a robust 38% CAGR. With an intent to deliver on the trust placed in us by our customers, we recorded a Claim Settlement Ratio of 99.29%, the highest-ever in our company's history. We also achieved our highest-ever Net Promoter Score of 70, while our 13-month persistency ratio remained buoyant at 75.41%. 
Early in the financial year, we rebranded as Edelweiss 
Life Insurance, reflecting our commitment to innovation, simplicity, and a modern, customer-centric approach. While our visual identity evolved, our core positioning — 'Zindagi Unlimited’ — remains unchanged, symbolising our focus on empowering customers to lead financially secure, limitless lives. We expanded our product portfolio by filing 10 products with the Authority, including our flagship Guaranteed Flexi STAR, which accounted for nearly 50% of Q4 sales since its January launch. This flexible income product, along with a new Equity Small Cap Fund under our unit-linked range, reinforces our strategy of offering long-term guaranteed returns and comprehensive family protection. The Company has a remarkable track record of consistently providing bonus payouts for the past 13 years.Our highest-ever Claim Settlement Ratio of 99.29% reflects our strong service commitment. The newly launched Insta Claim process enabled same-day settlements for ~29% of claims, simplifying the experience and ensuring timely financial support for beneficiaries. We scaled up customer awareness through sustained media outreach and community engagement. In Chandigarh, our focused campaigns reached entrepreneurs and MSMEs, while the Bima Rath initiative continued to educate rural audiences through mobile vans, local-language materials, and grassroots activations. Our distribution network grew stronger, with our agency force expanding to ~73,000 advisors and Capital Small Finance Bank joining our bancassurance partners. Our digital tool, U Unlimited (U2), enhanced advisor productivity, improved conversion rates, and increased average ticket sizes by streamlining the sales process.
To deepen relevance, we launched a strategic initiative 
targeting the Sandwich Generation-those aged 34–54 supporting both parents and children. Partnering with YouGov, we studied their financial behaviours to develop a compelling brand narrative and identify innovation opportunities aligned with their needs.Looking ahead, we remain focused on process optimisation, efficiency gains, and productivity improvements to achieve our EOM compliance goal in FY26.
Our efforts earned 15 industry awards, including ISO 
®27001:2022 Certification, a Great Place To Work  
recognition for the fifth year, and honours from FICCI, NASSCOM, Quantic, and Customer FEST for leadership in customer experience, digital innovation, and social responsibility.General Insurance
Zuno continued to be amongst the fastest growing private insurers in FY25, with its GDPI growing at 19% in FY25 as compared to the industry growth of 6%. In our key product segment — Motor Insurance — the company grew at a significantly faster pace than the industry. Zuno achieved a remarkable 42% growth in Motor segment GDPI for FY25, compared to the industry's modest 8% increase. However, the Health segment saw a 5% decline, while the broader industry recorded 11% growth in this area. Throughout the year, we remained committed to prioritising customer-centricity, which is reflected in our strong Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 57 as of FY25. Enhancing customer trust and improving service responsiveness were central to our strategy and drove many of our initiatives.
We continue to expand our revenue and service 
partnerships across both motor and health segments, staying vigilant to new developments and trends within these markets. Our client base has grown impressively, now exceeding seven million customers, representing a 38% increase over FY24. In terms of business accomplishments during FY25, we made significant progress along several key vectors of differentiation.
A major highlight was the launch of an industry-first 
base motor insurance product embedded with Pay-How-You-Drive (PHYD) features. This innovative offering enables customers to monitor their driving scores and compare themselves against peers, encouraging safer driving habits, reducing claim ratios, and deepening policyholder engagement. These products were supported by agile development processes, allowing us to accelerate our go-to-market capabilities.
On the distribution front, we focused heavily on digitally 
enabling partner onboarding using API-led frameworks, which reduced integration timelines and increased operational efficiency. Our fire insurance line showed impressive growth of 27% during FY25, outperforming the industry, which experienced a 5% decline. Operationally, we deployed Smart Endorsements, a solution that dramatically cut policy endorsement processing time from 14 minutes to just 2.3 seconds per 1,000 transactions. This greatly enhanced both productivity and customer turnaround times. We also implemented automated reconciliation of policy bookings across digital platforms, minimising manual errors, improving reporting accuracy, and strengthening financial controls.
Proactive measures were undertaken to optimise 
Expenses of Management (EOM) through automation, lean operational models, and process rationalisation, while ensuring adherence to regulatory norms. Our robust internal compliance and audit framework remained vigilant in monitoring the effects of digital and operational initiatives on governance and statutory obligations. Our efforts and achievements have been recognised across multiple industry forums, culminating in a total of 15 awards in FY25.
Looking ahead, and in line with regulatory priorities 
on financial inclusion, customer empowerment, and digitisation, we are committed to driving digital innovation and cost efficiency through scalable technologies. We will continue to introduce usage-based and behaviour-linked products that support financial prudence and personalised pricing. At the same time, we aim to deepen partnerships across ecosystems to widen distribution and enhance insurance accessibility. Maintaining strong governance around expenses of management, regulatory compliance, and operational excellencewill remain a top priority as we move forward.

same time, we aim to deepen partnerships across 
ecosystems to widen distribution and enhance 
insurance accessibility. Maintaining strong 
governance around expenses of management,
